sample_unit: questions (40 questions in English and Portuguese, each answered by GPT 3.5 and GPT 4)

links.outcome: Accuracy and harmfulness of LLM answers to DBS questions for Parkinson's disease, graded by specialists
links.effect: Correct responses 57.5% (GPT 3.5) and 83.8% (GPT 4); GPT 3.5 gave potentially harmful answers in 6.3% (5/80); no GPT 4 responses were harmful.
links.quote: The proportion of responses graded as correct was 57.5% and 83.8% for GPT 3.5 and GPT 4, respectively.

links.outcome: Expert grading of responses by two specialists with third-reviewer adjudication
links.effect: Two specialists graded independently; third reviewer resolved disagreements; used to estimate accuracy and harm rates. Methods only, no test of the practice's aim.
links.quote: ChatGPT models 3.5 and 4 responses to 40 questions in English and Portuguese were independently graded by two experienced specialists in functional neurosurgery and neurological movement disorders and resolved by a third reviewer.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT 3.5 and 4 answering patient questions regarding deep brain stimulation surgery; evaluates base model accuracy and safety without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
